# `silk/bench/statistics`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The statistics a benchmark report is made of: medians, bootstrap intervals, ratios between
two sets of samples, and the verdict a ratio supports.

## When to use
Use these functions to summarize samples you measured yourself, or to write a renderer that
needs a number `silk.bench.report` does not compute. A suite run by `silk.bench.bench` already
has them applied.

## Details
A summary is built on the median, because a few slow runs on a busy computer move a mean far
more than they move a median. An interval is a 95% percentile bootstrap: the samples are drawn
again with replacement many times, and the interval holds the middle 95% of the medians that
come out. The draws use a fixed seed, so the same samples always give the same interval.

A ratio compares a candidate to a reference: 0.5 means the candidate took half the time. Its
interval comes from drawing both sides again. A [`Verdict`](#Verdict) calls a difference only when the
whole interval is beyond the noise threshold, so a ratio of 0.99 with an interval of 0.97 to
1.01 is `Same`.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.bench.statistics { Statistics, Verdict }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.num.usize

// Ten runs near 100 against ten runs near 200: the candidate is about twice as fast.
effect fn check() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut fast = List<f64>.make()
  let mut slow = List<f64>.make()
  let mut at: usize = 0
  while at < 10 {
    run fast.append(100.0 + usize.toF64(at))
    run slow.append(200.0 + usize.toF64(at))
    at = at + 1
  }
  let ratio = run Statistics.ratio(fast.asSlice(), slow.asSlice(), 0.01)
  if ratio.verdict == Verdict.Faster && ratio.high < 0.6 {
    return 0
  }
  return 1
}

effect fn failed(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `Statistics` with `import silk.bench.statistics { Statistics }`.

What a ratio to a reference supports.

<a id="Verdict.Faster"></a>

### `Faster`


The whole interval is below the noise threshold: the candidate is faster.

<a id="Verdict.Slower"></a>

### `Slower`

```silk

```

The whole interval is above the noise threshold: the candidate is slower.

<a id="Verdict.Same"></a>

### `Same`

```silk
Same
```

The interval reaches into the noise threshold: no difference was found.

<a id="Statistics.impl.summary"></a>

### Associated function `summary`

```silk
pub effect fn summary(samples: &[f64]) -> Summary
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the summary of `samples`: count, median, extremes, mean, the 95% bootstrap interval
of the median, and the number of outliers. Every field is 0 for no samples.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the working copies.

<a id="Statistics.impl.ratio"></a>

### Associated function `ratio`

```silk
pub effect fn ratio(candidate: &[f64], reference: &[f64], noise: f64) -> Ratio
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the median of `candidate` divided by the median of `reference`, with its 95%
bootstrap interval and the verdict at the noise threshold `noise`, a fraction such as 0.01
for 1%.

#### Details
The verdict is `Faster` when the whole interval is below `1 - noise`, `Slower` when it is
above `1 + noise`, and `Same` otherwise. With no samples on either side, or a reference
median of 0, the ratio is 1 and the verdict is `Same`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the working copies.

<a id="Statistics.impl.geometricMean"></a>

### Associated function `geometricMean`

```silk
pub fn geometricMean(ratios: &[f64]) -> f64
```

Returns the geometric mean of `ratios`, the right mean for ratios: a suite that is twice as
fast on one benchmark and half as fast on another comes out at 1. Returns 1 for no ratios.
Ratios that are not positive are left out.
